newsitem.title: USA: ISDA sees US futures bill benefiting equity swaps.
newsitem.headline: ISDA sees US futures bill benefiting equity swaps.

text.p: International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) chairman Gay Evans said a bill on futures trading pending in the U.S. Senate would provide greater legal certainty for swaps, notably for equity swaps.

The bill to revise the Commodity Exchange Act (CEA) would make clearer that the Act would not apply to swaps, including equity swaps, Evans said in a prepared testimony before the Senate's Agriculture, Nutrition and Forestry Committee.
"We are particularly pleased that the bill extends the same legal certainty to swaps based on securities prices," she said.
"Equity swaps, like other swaps, enhance market efficiency, promote liquidity and allow investors to better manage their risk exposures," she added.

She noted that although both Congress and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) have recognised that swaps were "not appropriately regulated as futures under the Act", uncertainties have continued, particularly with equity swaps.

Although the bill had been introduced largely in response to U.S. futures exchanges' complaints that they were being handicapped against the over-the-counter market because of regulatory burden, Evans said ISDA welcomed it.
"While we, and others, will of course seek changes as the legislative process goes forward, ISDA supports this bill in principle," she said.

But Evans also reiterated ISDA's opposition to proposed modification to the so-called Treasury Amendment of 1974, which broadly exempts OTC transactions from CFTC jurisdiction and has caused some controversy involving foreign currency trading.

"ISDA continues to be skeptical of efforts to modify the Treasury Amendment to expand the CFTC's jurisdiction," she said. "We are concerned that any expansion of CFTC jurisdiction in this area could, unlike other provisions of the bill, ultimately lead to greater legal uncertainty."
She noted that provisions in the bill resolved some of the interpretive issues as to the applicability of the Treasury Amendment to foreign currency options.
Evans added that ISDA supported the Treasury's view the CFTC jurisdiction did not extend to the when-issued government securities markets.
